title: Disentangling the percepts of illusory movement and sensory stimulation during tendon vibration in the EEG

funding_references.funder_name: This work was supported by the Fondation CHUV, Lausanne, Switzerland; the Loterie Romande, Lausanne, Switzerland; and Techno Concept, Mane, France.

funding_references.award_title: Disentangling the percepts of illusory movement and sensory stimulation during tendon vibration in the EEG

description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 20 healthy participants during tendon vibration stimulation designed to elicit motor illusions. The study investigates the neural correlates of illusory movement perception versus pure sensory stimulation by comparing two vibration conditions: one inducing elbow extension illusions (biceps at 90 Hz, triceps at 50 Hz) and a control condition producing only vibration sensation (both tendons at 70 Hz). EEG was recorded from 16 electrodes covering sensorimotor cortex during three blocks of randomized stimulation sequences. This dataset is currently unpublished.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a g.tec Nautilus wireless system with 16 electrodes positioned over sensorimotor cortex (10-10 system: Fz, FC3, FC2, FCz, FC4, C3, C1, Cz, C2, C4, CP3, CP1, CPz, CP2, CP4) at 500 Hz sampling rate with 0.1-100 Hz bandpass filtering. Tendon vibration was delivered via wireless electromechanical vibrators (Vibramoov) placed on distal biceps and triceps tendons of the left arm. Stimulation consisted of three-second sequences with 1-second linear ramps and 1-second stable frequency intervals. Each participant completed three blocks of 72 vibrations (36 illusion, 36 control) with randomized inter-stimulus intervals (1-3 seconds).
